prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas exactly TWO equal cells side by side, FRONT then REAR, of the same small gated stone bridge shown in the attached labeled source/reference contact. The canonical source controls all material, colors, ornament, and identity; accepted TOP and RIGHT/LEFT show the real plan and low parapet height. True axis-aligned orthographic principal views only: camera looks horizontally straight toward the FRONT end for the first cell and horizontally straight toward the opposite REAR end for the second; no isometric, no perspective, no foreshortened 3D corner views.

Critical geometry: the bridge extends away along map depth. Its top plan shows three masonry sections along that length; those are separate longitudinal sections, NOT three vertically stacked stone blocks. The end elevations must be low and shallow, matching the accepted RIGHT/LEFT parapet height (approximately 60 pixels at final 256px sprite scale), with only two compact stone endcaps/piers at ground level, a short horizontal dark iron gate beam and narrow vertical iron gate bars where the gate is visible. Show only the thin edge of the bridge deck/walkway at that end; do not show its broad decorated top face. Never turn the three longitudinal masonry sections into tall Z pillars. No towering sidewalls, no full-height vertical deck rectangle, no frontal overhead plan, no tilted walkway.

FRONT is the gated approach: compact paired stone endcaps, dark iron gate bars/beam centered between them, and a very shallow deck edge beneath. REAR is the opposite end: compact paired stone endcaps and low source-matching horizontal parapet/beam silhouette, with only the small far-end gate structure if visible in the canonical source. Preserve recognizable pale sandstone blocks, charcoal mortar, subdued iron, and the authentic bridge design. Keep the silhouette centered and fully within each cell with generous transparent margins. No labels, shadows, stray guide marks, neighboring-cell bleed, extra posts or invented ornaments. Crisp clustered pixel art consistent with the source.
